title: The actual continuous coefficient inverse-image adjunct is invertible
statement: Let g:Y→X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] in universe u and T:Type u a totally disconnected topological commutative ring. Let T_X and T_Y denote the continuous-function coefficient sheaves [def-sfb-continuous-lattice-coefficients]. The canonical map g^{-1}T_X→T_Y, defined as the adjunct of precomposition with Y×_X U→U [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module], is an isomorphism of commutative-ring sheaves. This is a statement about that specified adjunct, without a choice of coefficient identification.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace, restriction of the continuous-coefficient lattice; canonical comparison argument of parent proof step 1.

proof.text: Identify the underlying additive coefficient sheaf with the universe-polymorphic condensed continuous-ring realization. The two explicit presentations of continuous functions have an identity comparison. Naturality along g follows by applying the chart-adjunction pasting formula: both adjoints precompose with Y[K]→X[K]→K.

The condensed pullback comparison is the invertible composition comparison. By the naturality square and invertibility of both continuous realizations, the additive adjunct of the specified coefficient direct-image map is invertible.

Forgetting commutative rings and forgetting abelian groups commute with the filtered left Kan extensions and sheafification defining inverse image. Use their unit-normalized comparisons to show that the underlying set map of the ring adjunct is conjugate to that of the additive adjunct. The set map is invertible, and forgetful functors reflect isomorphisms.
